user.title: LAN Guardian
user.description: Network to watch. Only IPv4 subnets up to /22 are supported.

data_description.gateway: The router address, used for latency and loss checks.

error.subnet_too_large: Subnet too large: use /22 or smaller.
error.gateway_outside_subnet: The gateway is not inside the subnet.

data_description.random_mac_mode: Phones rotate their MAC: group them in one entry, ignore them, or track each one as a device.

data.adblock_test_domain: Ad domain that must be blocked
data.shelly_warn_no_password: Warn about Shelly devices without password

data_description.dns_servers: The first one is the primary DNS: an issue is raised if it stops answering. If empty, the gateway is checked.
data_description.adblock_test_domain: Leave empty to skip the Pi-hole blocking check.
data_description.security_interval_hours: Looks for Tasmota and Shelly devices over HTTP and reports those without a password.
data_description.shelly_warn_no_password: Raises a security issue listing the Shelly devices whose local API accepts commands without authentication.

data.tasmota_import_mqtt: Import Tasmota devices from the MQTT integration
data.tasmota_warn_no_password: Warn about Tasmota devices without WebPassword

data_description.tasmota_password: Used for devices with a WebPassword (user admin) and applied to those without one. 8 to 32 characters, no spaces or ';'. Leave empty to keep the current one. Never logged.
data_description.tasmota_signal_drop: Percentage points the signal must lose against its usual level (average of the last 24 hours) to raise an alert.
data_description.tasmota_import_mqtt: Adds devices known to the official tasmota integration, even if the HTTP scan did not find them.
data_description.tasmota_warn_no_password: Raises a security issue listing the Tasmota devices that accept commands without a password.
data_description.generate_password: Creates a strong password, shows it once and stores it. Then apply it to the devices with the lan_guardian.apply_tasmota_password action or from the security issue.

data_description.notify_entities: Messages are sent with notify.send_message (for example the Telegram bot entity).
data_description.notify_service: Optional legacy action, for example notify.mobile_app_phone.

tasmota_device.title: Password of a single Tasmota
tasmota_device.description: Overrides the global password for one device. Leave empty to go back to the global one. 🔑 = dedicated password already set.

tasmota_password_generated.title: Generated password
tasmota_password_generated.description:
New WebPassword: **{password}**

Copy it somewhere safe now: it will not be shown again. You need it to open the Tasmota web UI (user `admin`). Confirm to store it.

error.invalid_host: Not a valid host name or IP address.
error.invalid_service: Use the domain.action format, for example notify.mobile_app_phone.
error.password_chars: Printable ASCII only, no spaces or ';'.

abort.no_tasmota: No Tasmota found yet: wait for the first scan.

data_description.critical: Alert when it stays offline and enable its connectivity sensor.

abort.device_gone: The device is no longer in the inventory.

critical_offline.title: Critical device offline: {name}
critical_offline.description: {name} ({ip}, {mac}) has not answered since {last_seen}. Check power and Wi-Fi signal. The issue closes by itself when it is back online.

mac_multiple_ips.title: MAC on several IP addresses: {name}
mac_multiple_ips.description: {mac} answers on {ips}. It may be a legitimate bridge or repeater, but also ARP spoofing. The issue closes when the MAC is back on a single IP.

confirm.title: Accept the new gateway MAC
confirm.description: Gateway {ip} answers with {current} instead of {previous}. Confirm only if you replaced or reset the router: otherwise someone may be intercepting traffic (ARP spoofing).

dns_primary_down.title: Primary DNS {server} is not answering
dns_primary_down.description: DNS server {server} has not answered for at least two checks. Devices using it (the whole network, if DHCP hands it out) cannot resolve names. Check the DNS server.

gateway_packet_loss.title: Packet loss towards the gateway
gateway_packet_loss.description: {loss}% loss towards {ip} (threshold {threshold}%) for at least two checks. Check Home Assistant's network cable and the router load.

adblock_inactive.title: Pi-hole is not blocking ads
adblock_inactive.description: {server} resolves {domain} to {addresses}. Blocking may be disabled or the lists out of date.

confirm.title: Set the WebPassword
confirm.description:
These devices accept any HTTP command from anyone on the network, including restart, reset and firmware upload: {devices}.

The password stored in LAN Guardian will be set on {count} devices: {devices}.

MQTT and the Tasmota integration are not affected; the web UI will ask for user `admin` and the password. The outcome arrives as a notification.

abort.no_password: First store a WebPassword in Options → Tasmota (type or generate one), then come back here.

shelly_no_password.title: {count} Shelly devices without password
shelly_no_password.description:
These Shelly devices accept any local command from anyone on the network, including switching, reset and firmware update: {devices}.

Set a password in each device's web UI (Settings → Authentication) or in the Shelly app. Then update the credentials in Home Assistant's Shelly integration, which will ask for them. The issue closes on the next security check.

tasmota_signal_drop.title: Tasmota Wi-Fi signal dropped
tasmota_signal_drop.description: Signal dropped by {threshold} points or more against its usual level (usual → recent): {devices}. Check the access point or repeater the device connects to and anything that moved near it. The usual level adapts within about a day, so a lasting change stops being reported.

tasmota_frequent_restarts.title: {name} restarts often
tasmota_frequent_restarts.description: {name} ({ip}) restarted {count} times in the last 24 hours. Last reason: {reason}. Typical causes: unstable power supply, watchdog on weak Wi-Fi, firmware exceptions.

tasmota_auth_failed.title: Tasmota password rejected
tasmota_auth_failed.description: These devices answer 401 with the configured password: {devices}. Set the right password in LAN Guardian's Tasmota options (global or per device).

update_device.name: Update device
update_device.description: Change name, category, critical flag or status of an inventory device.

forget_device.name: Forget device
forget_device.description: Remove the device from the inventory: if it shows up again it will be new.

backup_tasmota.name: Backup Tasmota
backup_tasmota.description: Download the configuration of the chosen Tasmota devices now (all of them if none is chosen). Backups identical to the previous one are not written again.

apply_tasmota_password.name: Set Tasmota WebPassword
apply_tasmota_password.description: Sets the password stored in LAN Guardian's options on the chosen Tasmota devices (all of them if none is chosen). Skips protected ones; the password is not a parameter, so it never reaches the database.

device_id.name: Devices
device_id.description: Tasmota devices to set it on.

unknown_device.message: No device with MAC {mac} in the inventory.

no_password.message: No WebPassword stored: set one in Options → Tasmota.

firmware_unsupported.message: {name} cannot be updated from here: development or self-built firmware, unknown image, or latest release not yet known.
